opportunity: The `decompile-all --json` `variables` surface spelled a one-byte value the type system never committed to `char` -- what the printer emits for the residual TYPE_UNKNOWN carrier under the default `realtypes`. On a machine-readable surface that asserts an element type the recovery never established (the program's own type may as well be `_Bool`, `unsigned char`, a one-byte enum or one byte of an unsplit struct). Ghidra reports the same fact as `undefined1`, IDA as `_BYTE`, and kuna's own framelayout section already reported an uncommitted frame slot as `undefined<N>` -- so one array reported the same fact two different ways.
test_name: kuna-console verify_bytehonest (two-pass e2e over every function of the vendored fauxware) + 5 hermetic predicate unit tests + the tests/cli two-pass probe pair
inspiration: Ghidra's `undefined1` and IDA's `_BYTE` for the same fact; kuna's own `framelayout` frame-slot speller (`undefined<N>`)

predicate.rule: metatype == TYPE_UNKNOWN && size == 1, read off the Rc<Datatype>, never off its printed spelling
predicate.sections: extract_variables 1 (FuncProto parameters) and 2 (ScopeLocal NO_CATEGORY stack symbols); section 3 keeps its own wider framelayout rule
predicate.never: an array of unknown (a char[264] local must keep its array-ness; `undefined264` would drop it and match nothing), any size other than 1, any committed metatype
predicate.exported_size: unchanged -- the datatype's own size, so every re-spelled row reports size 1
predicate.realtypes_independent: with realtypes off the same row exports the internal `xunknown1`; the predicate reads the datatype, so `undefined1` is exported there too

benchmark.corpus: frozen decbench C corpus (results/full_run_address_2026-09-11), O0 + O2, scored with scripts.decbench.typesweep, DECBENCH_NO_CACHE=1, KUNA_BIN pinned to this branch's release build
benchmark.arms: the sweep's `base` arm is this build's DEFAULT (bytehonest ON) and its `test` arm is `--option bytehonest off`; the fields below are relabelled accordingly (perfect_off = the OFF arm)
benchmark.control: baseline vs published type_match 5045 agree / 253 differ (95.2% agreement; the residue is kuna-build drift since the tree was scored, not this option)
benchmark.note: `improved` counts every function whose score rose, the 10 that rose to a perfect 1.000 included. 0 functions scored lower anywhere in the 5,298.
benchmark.zero_regressed_is_empirical: type_match's claim() is greedy: for each ground-truth variable, in a fixed arg -> offset -> name pass order, it takes the FIRST matching unused candidate and never reconsiders that claim (decbench/metrics/type_match.py:1041). Widening what a candidate matches can therefore in principle let one ground-truth variable consume a candidate a later one would have matched better. `0 worse` over 5,298 scored functions is a measurement, not a structural guarantee -- the metric cannot prove no such reordering exists, only that none occurred here.

speed.note: the box is shared with concurrent agents (load average 20-50 during the run): individual paired deltas span -21% to +24%, so the paired median and the min-of-15 are the statistics that mean anything. Both are flat, which is what the mechanism predicts -- one metatype+size comparison per exported variable row, on a surface that is built after the decompile is finished.

notes: The C text and the JSON surface disagree on purpose for exactly this carrier: `char a0` in the .c, `undefined1` in `variables[]`. The C text must be legal C and `undefined1` is not a C type; `variables[]` is a report of what the recovery established. Written down in docs/spec/06-variables-and-merge.md §6.2.
